meta.tagline: chase the invoice so you do not have to
meta.description: Polite, automatic invoice reminders for freelancers. Connects to the invoices you already send and follows up until you are paid.

hero.headline: The invoice is not late. You just stopped asking.
hero.sub: Tallystone follows up on unpaid invoices on a schedule you set, in wording you would actually send, and stops the moment the money lands.
hero.note: No card to start. Cancel from the account page in two clicks.
trust: Works with the invoices you already send

sections.heading: Freelancers do not have a collections department
sections.intro: They have a nagging feeling on a Sunday night and a client who has gone quiet.

items.title: Follows up on a schedule
items.body: Day 3 after due, day 10, day 21, then monthly. Or whatever cadence you set. It does not get embarrassed and it does not forget.

items.title: Sounds like you
items.body: Three tones — friendly, firm, final. You edit the wording once and every future reminder uses it.

items.title: Stops on payment
items.body: Mark it paid, or let the bank import do it. Nothing more goes out. Nobody gets chased for money they already sent.

items.title: Shows what is owed
items.body: One screen: what is outstanding, how old it is, and who has been reminded how many times.

items.title: Escalates on your say-so
items.body: Past a threshold you choose, it drafts the firmer message and waits for you to press send.

items.title: Keeps the paper trail
items.body: Every reminder is logged with its date and wording, which is what you need if it ever goes further.

items.title: Point it at your invoices
items.body: Forward them to a Tallystone address, or upload a CSV from whatever you bill with.

items.title: Set the schedule and the tone
items.body: Pick a cadence, edit the three templates until they sound like you rather than like software.

items.title: Let it run
items.body: It sends, logs and stops on payment. You get one weekly summary and nothing else.

sections.heading: One plan, in Canadian dollars
sections.intro: No per-seat pricing, no usage tiers, no annual lock-in.

tiers.name: Tallystone
tiers.desc: Unlimited invoices, unlimited reminders, one person.
tiers.fine: Cancel any time. No refund needed because you are never billed for a month you did not use.

items.a: A reminder about an invoice they agreed to pay is not annoying, and the tone is yours to set. Most people who go quiet are not refusing to pay — they lost the email.

items.q: Does it replace my invoicing tool?
items.a: No. It sits behind whatever you already use and handles only the part everybody avoids.
Reminders stop, and you can export everything as CSV. Your data is not held hostage to make leaving hard.

items.q: Is my client list used for anything else?
items.a: No. It is not sold, not used for advertising and not used to train anything.

sections.heading: Thirty days free. No card.
sections.intro: If it has not collected something by day 30, it has not earned CAD 12.

legal.deliverable: the Tallystone subscription described on this site
collects: The email address and account details you enter when signing up, and the invoice data you choose to send in.
Nothing is collected by simply reading this page: no analytics, no advertising, no cookies.
legal.refund: Billing is monthly and cancelling stops the next charge immediately, so there is nothing to claw back. If a charge went out after you cancelled, say so and it is returned.

footer.note: Sample build. Tallystone is a fictional product invented to demonstrate the template — the features, the price and the checkout link are not real.
